subject: Materials Science
title: Thermoelectric Materials
description: A fast breakdown of Thermoelectric Materials for builders.

hook.text: Put a temperature difference across a semiconductor and it generates electricity — no turbine, no moving parts.

buildup.text: The Seebeck effect drives charge carriers from hot to cold — creating voltage proportional to the temperature gradient.

discovery.text: Bismuth telluride (Bi₂Te₃) is the champion near room temperature — used in portable coolers and waste heat recovery.

twist.text: Efficiency is low — only 5–10% — because materials that conduct electricity also conduct heat, fighting the gradient.

climax.text: NASA's Voyager probes have run on thermoelectric generators since 1977 — still sending data from interstellar space.

punchline.text: Heat in, electricity out — semiconductors can harvest temperature differences.

quiz.question: What limits thermoelectric efficiency?
options: Materials can only work at extreme temperatures
Good electrical conductors also conduct heat, reducing the temperature gradient
Thermoelectric materials are too rare to use
